body:
Richt is a standalone Go CLI for executable host configuration plans. Describe hosts and reusable services in YAML, inspect the resolved inventory, prepare changes against the targets, then review and explicitly apply them. Services combine RPM packages, templated files, and systemd processes. Config-only, package-only, and process-only services are also supported.
Start with the config-only quickstart , then use installation and platform requirements and the CLI reference for your environment. The examples include ready-package vmango, SSH, local secrets, and deliberate failure/continuation scenarios. Validation separates recorded Linux acceptance from illustrative configurations.
The focused contracts are:
Inventory : strict YAML, tag assignments and variable order, paths, ordering, ownership, and filters. Files and saved plans : templates, attributes, SELinux, confirmation, executable JSON, and locking. RPM and systemd : exact versions, reactions, timeouts, unit files, and removal. SSH and sudo : client configuration, authentication, privileges, and parallel hosts. Secrets : source lookup, sensitive display, and real saved bytes. Continuation : task progress, partial failure, and explicit retry using the same plan. Read limitations before using a saved plan as an operational artifact. Plans contain prepared executable inputs, potentially including secrets; apply does not recompute changes or check targets for drift.

body:
Build with make build and run from the repository root. This example manages only /var/tmp/richt-example/greeting.conf; it needs no root, RPM, systemd or network access when that directory is writable by the current user.
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/files/inventory.yaml bin/richt diff -i examples/files/inventory.yaml -o /var/tmp/richt-files-plan.json bin/richt apply -y /var/tmp/richt-files-plan.json cat /var/tmp/richt-example/greeting.conf bin/richt diff -i examples/files/inventory.yaml Diff renders and observes without modifying managed resources; saving a plan writes only that plan. The final diff should have no changes. Change greeting in the inventory to inspect an update. Apply without -y for explicit terminal confirmation; piped input does not supply terminal agreement.
Set tags.example.services.greeting.state: absent, prepare a new plan and apply it to remove the managed file. Removing the assignment alone requests no deletion. Restore state: present afterwards if reusing the checked-in example. The containing directory, plan and lock are retained. Use the continuation walkthrough for a repeatable failure that demonstrates saved progress and manual resume.
See files and saved plans for frozen inputs, confirmation, locking, attributes and sensitive output, and the repository acceptance report for executed validation results.

title: Local files

body:
This walkthrough uses one local host and a config-only service. Run it from the repository root on Linux with Go 1.27.3 or newer, Make, and standard shell tools. It creates all managed targets in a fresh private temporary directory and needs no root, DNF, systemd, or network access after building. Full Linux platform requirements and verification scope are in installation and validation .
Build and describe the file make build ./bin/richt --version demo_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/richt-quickstart.XXXXXX") chmod 700 "$demo_dir" printf '%s\n' 'message={{ .greeting }}' > "$demo_dir/greeting.gotmpl" cat > "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" <<EOF_INVENTORY tags: defaults: order: 10 services: greeting: {state: present} vars: greeting: Hello from Richt services: greeting: order: 10 configs: main: path: $demo_dir/target/greeting.conf mode: "0644" template: {file: greeting.gotmpl} hosts: - name: local tags: [defaults] transport: {type: local} EOF_INVENTORY Keep this shell open so demo_dir stays available. Tag defaults assigns the service and supplies the template’s .greeting variable. The service definition’s order fixes execution order; config-only services need no binary or process component. Template paths are relative to their declaring service file, or the inventory for inline services.
Inspect, prepare, and apply ./bin/richt inventory validate -i "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" ./bin/richt inventory show -i "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" ./bin/richt diff -i "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" -o "$demo_dir/create.json" ./bin/richt apply "$demo_dir/create.json" cat "$demo_dir/target/greeting.conf" ./bin/richt diff -i "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" Inventory inspection does not read templates or contact the host. Diff renders the template and observes the target, then displays the planned file write and attributes. It does not change managed resources. Review the display and type yes at apply’s terminal prompt. The resulting file contains message=Hello from Richt; the final diff reports no changes.
In a noninteractive shell, use ./bin/richt apply -y "$demo_dir/create.json" when you intend to skip confirmation. Piping yes into apply does not satisfy the terminal requirement. The saved JSON contains executable prepared inputs and task progress; apply does not reread the source files or recalculate the diff. Keep saved plans private, especially when templates use secrets.
Update and explicitly remove printf '%s\n' 'message={{ .greeting }} (updated)' > "$demo_dir/greeting.gotmpl" ./bin/richt diff -i "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" -o "$demo_dir/update.json" ./bin/richt apply "$demo_dir/update.json" cat "$demo_dir/target/greeting.conf" sed 's/state: present/state: absent/' "$demo_dir/inventory.yaml" > "$demo_dir/remove.yaml" ./bin/richt diff -i "$demo_dir/remove.yaml" -o "$demo_dir/remove.json" ./bin/richt apply "$demo_dir/remove.json" test ! -e "$demo_dir/target/greeting.conf" The update changes the file to message=Hello from Richt (updated). Explicit state: absent removes the declared file. Deleting an assignment alone does not request removal. Removal does not render templates or read secret sources, and leaves the parent directory in place.
To remove this walkthrough’s remaining inputs and plans after reviewing them:
rm -rf -- "$demo_dir" Continue with inventory rules , the ready-package vmango example , SSH , or the two-source secret example . To see a partial failure and retry only unfinished work, use the continuation walkthrough .

body:
Build from source Obtain a checkout with Git, then run the build commands from its root:
git clone https://github.com/subuk/richt.git cd richt Building requires Go 1.27.3 or newer and Make. Go downloads the dependencies pinned in go.mod and verified by go.sum when they are not already cached.
make build ./bin/richt --help ./bin/richt --version make install make build writes bin/richt. make install writes to GOBIN, or to $(go env GOPATH)/bin when GOBIN is unset; put that directory on PATH. To keep an installation in the checkout:
mkdir -p bin GOBIN="$PWD/bin" make install Development builds print richt dev. Set a label with make build VERSION=0.1.0; a label does not change plan compatibility. To build a static binary for a Linux amd64 target from another controller:
make linux-amd64 # Output: bin/richt-linux-amd64 These are source-build instructions. The repository does not require a Richt agent, central server, NetBox, or Argo CD.
Controllers and targets Role Requirements and verified scope Inventory inspection The Richt binary and local inventory/service YAML. It does not contact hosts or open templates or secret sources. Local file execution Filesystem access to the declared targets; named owners/groups must already exist. Linux acceptance covers ownership, permissions, symlinks, and SELinux. SSH controller Richt and system OpenSSH ssh in PATH; local template and secret files for preparation. macOS has been used as a controller. SSH target Linux shell and standard GNU coreutils/findutils, getent, plus the utilities needed by selected resources. No Go toolchain or Richt binary is needed there. RPM resources DNF 4, or YUM 4 backed by DNF 4, and an RPM database. Repository/network access is needed when DNF executes the transaction. Processes systemd with systemctl; declared units or packages that supply them. SELinux attributes An SELinux-enabled Linux target whose kernel accepts the requested full label. Requests fail explicitly on other systems. The recorded full-stack platform is AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64, DNF 4.20.0, YUM 4 compatibility, systemd 257, with file/label acceptance on SELinux Enforcing. Other distributions, versions, architectures, and package managers are not established by that result. A Linux cross-build proves compilation only. See validation for the exact scenarios and evidence.
Only selected resources need their backend capabilities. File-only use does not require DNF or systemd. Python 3 is used by repository example verifiers and acceptance harnesses; it is not required by the Richt CLI.
Privileges Run inventory commands as an ordinary user. Diff observes targets, so it needs read and observation access; it may fail on protected resources without suitable privileges. Apply needs permission to create parents, write/remove the managed files, set requested attributes, and run selected package/systemd operations. System configuration and RPM transactions normally require root.
Choose privileges explicitly in inventory:
transport: {type: local} # current user's privileges # Or: transport: {type: local, sudo: true} # execute through sudo -n # Or on a remote target: transport: {type: ssh, host: app-a, user: deploy, sudo: true} Richt never enables sudo implicitly. sudo: true uses noninteractive sudo -n for commands and file operations; configure authorization beforehand. SSH also runs without a terminal and cannot prompt for passwords, key passphrases, or host-key agreement. Set up keys/agent and host trust using your normal SSH workflow. apply -y skips only Richt’s plan confirmation. See the SSH guide for client aliases, overrides, and authentication behavior.
Use a disposable Linux target for package/process examples and acceptance. The quickstart confines its config-only targets to a newly created private directory and needs no root privileges.

This example illustrates tag service assignment, merging variables, service ordering, selections, service file paths, and fictional SSH settings. It is not an execution quickstart: lanst.example.invalid is a fictional address, its declared secret source files need not exist, and the local cloud assumes an existing libvirt hypervisor. Use the runnable Vmango walkthrough for an isolated RPM/systemd installation with no hypervisor.
Run from the repository root:
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml bin/richt inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml bin/richt inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml --tag hypervisor --service vmango These commands do not contact hosts, open templates, or read secret values. The hypervisor tag assigns both services; service definition orders 10 and 20 run the repository before Vmango. The home and net tags override only vmango.cloud_name; the shared listen address and libvirt URI remain. Adding both tags to one host causes a variable conflict at the same tag order. title: Inventory and variables

body:
Run richt --help or richt COMMAND --help for generated help. Examples below use richt on PATH; a source build is available as ./bin/richt. With no command, Richt prints help. richt --version prints the build version.
Command Behavior richt inventory validate [selection] Load and validate YAML, references, merged variables, selected assignments, and resource ownership. richt inventory show [selection] Perform the same validation and print resolved inventory as indented JSON. richt diff [selection] [-o PLAN.json] Prepare and display changes by observing targets; optionally save the executable JSON plan. richt apply [selection] [-y] [--parallelism N] Build, display, confirm, and apply a new plan; progress lives only in memory. richt apply PLAN.json [-y] [--parallelism N] Display, confirm, execute, and update a saved plan; continue unfinished tasks on a later explicit invocation. Inventory inspection never contacts hosts, opens templates, or reads secret sources. Diff can contact targets and read local templates/secrets; it does not modify managed resources. -o writes the plan file as an explicit output.
Inventory and selection flags Flag Meaning -i PATH, --inventory PATH YAML inventory; defaults to inventory.yaml in the current directory. --host NAME Select named hosts; repeat or comma-separate names. --tag NAME Select hosts carrying a tag; repeat or comma-separate names. --service NAME Select already assigned services; repeat or comma-separate names. Host names and tags form a union, repeated services form another union, and the two groups intersect. An unspecified group selects everything. Matching is exact and case sensitive; unknown names fail. Service selection does not add assignments or pull in prerequisite services. Full schema validation still includes unselected definitions and unused tag assignments. Every selected host uses all its tags; duplicate assignments, service-order collisions, ownership and variable conflicts cannot be hidden by a service filter. See inventory .
richt inventory show -i fleet.yaml --host app-a --tag staging --service web richt diff -i fleet.yaml --host app-a --service repository --service web -o plan.json richt apply -i fleet.yaml --tag staging --parallelism 2 -i, --host, --tag, and --service are argument errors with a saved plan. A saved plan already fixes its hosts and tasks. Build a new plan if you need a different selection.
Apply flags and results -y or --yes skips Richt’s confirmation prompt. Otherwise apply requires a terminal and explicit y or yes; empty/negative responses cancel. Piped input is not terminal agreement. The plan is displayed in both modes. This flag does not change privileges, SSH authentication, or compatibility/result checks.
--parallelism N accepts a positive integer and defaults to 20 simultaneous hosts. 1 runs hosts sequentially. The flag applies to both new and saved plans; it is execution configuration and does not rebuild tasks or change progress. Services/tasks remain sequential within a host. A failed task blocks that host’s remaining tasks while other hosts continue. See SSH and parallel apply for persistence and cancellation details.
The final report includes per-host completed, previously completed, failed, and blocked tasks, plus the saved path and manual continuation instruction when applicable. Forced termination can prevent a final report.
Successful commands exit 0. Kong argument-parsing errors exit 2; execution, validation, compatibility, cancellation, and task failures exit nonzero (currently 1). Do not infer success from a partial apply display: check the process exit status and final results.
richt apply -y --parallelism 2 plan.json # After fixing the cause of a failure, explicitly continue the same plan: richt apply -y --parallelism 1 plan.json There is no automatic saved plan for apply -i, separate progress store, retry, rollback, or run history. Use diff -o before applying when persistent continuation is required.

body:
Run this example on a disposable AlmaLinux 10 x86_64 machine with root, DNF 4, systemd as PID 1, network access to distribution repositories, EPEL and COPR, and a built Linux Richt binary at bin/richt. Run all commands from the repository root. The example owns /etc/yum.repos.d/richt-vmango.repo, /etc/vmango.conf, the vmango package and vmango.service; start without an existing Vmango installation or either managed configuration file.
It uses published, signed Vmango COPR RPMs . No package build, fixture repository, rpm-build, createrepo_c, or COPR CLI plugin is needed. The config-only repository service runs before the package service. The rhel-10 target is deliberate: EPEL 10 builds target CentOS Stream and can require newer libvirt than AlmaLinux/RHEL provides. Runtime dependencies are resolved by DNF during apply; no hypervisor or VM image is required.
The minimal application configuration binds only 127.0.0.1:18080, has no clouds/hosts or login users, and stores generated state below /var/lib/vmango. It demonstrates installation and process lifecycle, not VM provisioning or a usable authenticated deployment. The package supplies the service unit; its configuration changes use restart because no reload interface is assumed. Root ownership and mode 0644 let the package-created vmango user read the config without requiring that account to exist during first preparation.
Enable the standard AlmaLinux CRB and EPEL repositories before applying. The published package requires genisoimage, which was available through EPEL in the recorded AlmaLinux 10.2 run:
dnf config-manager --set-enabled crb dnf install -y epel-release These prepare dependency sources; Richt still installs Vmango and its runtime dependencies through the reviewed plan. Keep package signature checking enabled.
Inspect, install, and inspect again Inventory validation opens no templates, contacts no hosts and fetches no packages. The remaining commands observe or modify this disposable local host:
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml bin/richt inventory show -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml -o /root/vmango-install.json bin/richt apply -y /root/vmango-install.json rpm -q vmango systemctl is-active vmango.service systemctl is-enabled vmango.service curl --fail --silent --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:18080/ bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml The second diff should have no changes. Richt verifies systemd’s running state; the separate HTTP request checks that an HTTP response is served, without claiming application or hypervisor readiness. For startup diagnostics use journalctl -u vmango.service --no-pager -n 50.
Exact upgrade, downgrade, and config reaction The pinned initial version is 0:0.16.0-1.el10.x86_64. Repository primary metadata read on 2026-11-01 also contained 0:0.12.3-1.el10.x86_64, 0:0.15.0-1.el10.x86_64, and 0:0.17.0-1.el10.x86_64. Repository metadata is mutable; if a version is no longer available, inspect available published versions before selecting another compatible pair. Never replace this step with a locally built fixture RPM.
Edit examples/vmango/services/vmango.yaml: change the exact version from 0:0.16.0-1.el10.x86_64 to 0:0.17.0-1.el10.x86_64, then:
bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml -o /root/vmango-upgrade.json bin/richt apply -y /root/vmango-upgrade.json rpm -q vmango systemctl is-active vmango.service Change it back to 0:0.16.0-1.el10.x86_64 and repeat with a new plan path /root/vmango-downgrade.json. DNF’s exact installation request permits a downgrade as well as an upgrade. Omitting version instead keeps any installed version; it does not request the latest available package.
For a config-only change, record the service’s InvocationID, change log_level: info to log_level: debug in examples/vmango/inventory.yaml, prepare and apply a new plan, then compare:
systemctl show vmango.service -p InvocationID bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml -o /root/vmango-config.json bin/richt apply -y /root/vmango-config.json systemctl show vmango.service -p InvocationID bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml The diff displays the config change and restart branch. The invocation changes when the running process is restarted. A stopped process receives start only; there is no extra restart after that start. For failure/continuation without packages, use the separate config-only example .
Explicit removal Set state: absent on both assignments under tags.example.services in examples/vmango/inventory.yaml, keeping service definition orders 10 and 20. Then:
bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml -o /root/vmango-remove.json bin/richt apply -y /root/vmango-remove.json rpm -q vmango systemctl is-active vmango.service bin/richt diff -i examples/vmango/inventory.yaml The RPM query and active check are expected to return nonzero after removal. Richt removes the declared repository file, stops/disables the process, removes its config, then removes its package. Package removal uses the installed RPM database and does not require the removed repository file. A missing assignment alone never removes resources. Application state, package-manager dependencies, possible .rpmsave files, generated keys, imported RPM signing keys, and saved plans are not purged by Richt. Restore the example files’ original version, log level, and present assignments before another run.
Validation status: the published-package lifecycle passed on 2026-11-01 on AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 with DNF 4.20.0, systemd 257 and SELinux Enforcing. Install, no-op, unversioned preservation, exact upgrade/downgrade, config restart, independent stopped/enablement states and explicit removal were exercised. See the acceptance report for dependency prerequisites, evidence, cleanup and limits.

body:
This inventory reuses the Vmango example on two disposable AlmaLinux 10 x86_64 targets. Its richt-test-a and richt-test-b SSH aliases are placeholders. Configure each alias’s HostName, non-root User, authentication key/agent and trusted host key using normal OpenSSH settings. Both accounts need noninteractive sudo -n for the managed operations. Both targets need DNF 4, systemd, distribution repositories, CRB, EPEL and COPR network access; neither needs a compiler, fixture package build, hypervisor or Vmango login user. Prepare CRB and EPEL on each target with sudo -n dnf config-manager --set-enabled crb and sudo -n dnf install -y epel-release; the published RPM needs EPEL’s genisoimage dependency. Start without an existing Vmango installation or the example’s managed files. See SSH rules for explicit overrides and authentication.
From the repository root, inventory-only inspection is safe even before SSH is configured:
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/ssh/inventory.yaml bin/richt inventory show -i examples/ssh/inventory.yaml After replacing/configuring the aliases, check each connection, prepare once, then explicitly apply. The checks require no remote configuration changes:
ssh -o BatchMode=yes richt-test-a 'sudo -n true' ssh -o BatchMode=yes richt-test-b 'sudo -n true' bin/richt diff -i examples/ssh/inventory.yaml -o /var/tmp/richt-ssh-plan.json bin/richt apply -y --parallelism 2 /var/tmp/richt-ssh-plan.json bin/richt diff -i examples/ssh/inventory.yaml The second diff should have no changes. Hosts can run concurrently, while services/tasks remain ordered within each host. --parallelism 1 makes host execution sequential; the default limit is 20. A failed host blocks its later tasks while the other host continues. Fix the external problem, then apply the same saved plan explicitly to skip successful tasks and retry unfinished ones. No automatic retry occurs. Saved plans retain explicit inventory connections and ready config bytes; OpenSSH still reads current client configuration.
For cleanup, set both assignments in the shared tags.example.services map to state: absent, build a new removal plan and apply it. The Vmango walkthrough describes retained application data and RPM side effects. Do not delete assignments as a substitute for declaring absence.
Validation status: published Vmango installation/no-op/removal passed on two independent AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 targets on 2026-11-01 using non-root SSH, explicit sudo and --parallelism 2. A separate two-host secret/file scenario verified frozen inputs, host failure isolation and manual continuation. See the acceptance report for environment and limits.

body:
Validate and view the supplied two-host example without network access:
go run . inventory validate -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml go run . inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml go run . inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml --tag hypervisor --service vmango validate resolves the selected scope and reports errors. show performs the same checks and writes the resolved inventory as indented JSON. Neither command contacts hosts, opens templates, reads secret source values, or changes host state. The example describes a local host and an illustrative SSH host; execution supports both transport descriptions. See SSH and parallel apply for connection settings and noninteractive authentication.
The example resolves gena.vmango.cloud_name to Home and lanst.vmango.cloud_name to Net. Both retain listen = 127.0.0.1:8080 and libvirt_uri = qemu:///system. Each host’s services are ordered vmango-repository (10), then vmango (20), independent of YAML listing order.
Schema and file references Inventory contains tags, services, hosts, and optional secret_sources. Names of hosts, tags, services and components start with a letter or number and contain only letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Component names are stable keys, independent of resource paths, package names and unit names. Unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys, non-string mapping keys, and multiple YAML documents are errors. All definitions and references are validated, including definitions outside the selected scope.
tags: shared: order: 10 services: app: {} vars: app: listen: "127.0.0.1:8080" services: app: order: 10 file: services/app.yaml hosts: - name: example tags: [shared] transport: {type: local} secret_sources: default: {type: yaml, file: secrets/default.yaml} production: {type: yaml, file: secrets/production.yaml} A service requires an integer order, including when it is not assigned to any host. Explicit zero is valid; omission is an error. Components can be defined inline or by file, exclusively, with order beside either form. Referenced files contain one bare service definition (binaries, configs, processes), without another services wrapper or recursive file references. Service file paths are relative to the inventory file. Template paths are relative to the service file declaring them; inline services use the inventory file as their base. Absolute local file paths are also accepted. URL sources are unsupported. Resolved JSON includes absolute source/template paths and normalized absolute target paths.
A service must contain at least one component; binary-only, config-only and process-only services are accepted. Tags assign services through a mapping keyed by service name. Each value contains only optional state: present|absent; {} defaults to present. Hosts receive services from all their tags and do not declare assignments themselves. A host without assignments has an empty service list. Component parameters belong to the service definition, with no assignment or host overrides.
Each service must occur at most once on a host, even when two tags assign it with identical settings. Errors identify the host, service and both source tags. Different effective services on a host must have different service orders. Tags or services that are never combined on a host may reuse assignments or order values. Services execute in ascending service order, including absent assignments; tag order does not set execution order. Removing a tag or assignment does not request resource removal: use explicit state: absent.
Components binaries: package: type: rpm manager: dnf # dnf (default) or yum package: app version: "0:1.2-3.noarch" # optional exact epoch:version-release.arch configs: main: path: /etc/app.conf owner: root group: root mode: "0644" selinux: system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0 sensitive: false template: file: templates/app.gotmpl processes: web: type: systemd unit: app.service state: running # running (default) or stopped enabled: true # optional timeout: 5s # positive Go duration; default 5s restart_on: [binary.package] reload_on: [config.main] after: [] Configuration targets must be absolute file paths. mode is an octal string. template requires exactly one of file or inline; an empty inline string is valid. Templates receive the complete merged host variables. Missing variables, file permissions, actual owners/groups and SELinux application are checked when preparing or executing a plan, beyond inventory-only validation.
restart_on and reload_on reference binary.<name> or config.<name> in the same service. after references process names in the same service. Unknown, duplicate or cross-service references and cycles are errors. Processes use systemd .service unit names. Reload support depends on host capabilities and is checked during plan preparation.
An optional process unit_file and named overrides use the same fields as configs. Their target paths may be omitted and are then derived as shown:
processes: web: type: systemd unit: app.service unit_file: template: {file: templates/app.service.gotmpl} overrides: 10-runtime.conf: template: {inline: "[Service]\nRestart=always\n"} The unit target is /etc/systemd/system/app.service; the override target is /etc/systemd/system/app.service.d/10-runtime.conf. Explicit paths must match these locations. Override names are plain .conf filenames. Template paths still use the declaring service file as their base.
Variable merging Tags are processed by ascending order, which defaults to zero when omitted. All tags of an order are checked as a group before that group is merged with earlier orders. Host tag listing order has no effect.
Scalars and lists replace the lower-order value completely. Maps merge recursively; a map and a non-map replace each other at higher order. At equal order, different keys and compatible nested maps merge. Identical values are accepted. Different scalar/list values or incompatible types on the same path fail, even when a higher-order tag would replace that path. Errors identify the host, variable path, both tag names and common order. For a reproducible conflict, add home to lanst.tags in a copy of the example: home and net both set vmango.cloud_name at order 20. Validation fails at vars.vmango.cloud_name, including when --service vmango-repository is used.
Resource ownership Before service filtering, every assignment of each selected host is checked. Different services cannot own the same explicitly declared RPM package, normalized absolute file path, or systemd unit, even with identical settings or different present/absent states. DNF and YUM share the RPM package namespace. Managed unit files and drop-ins also claim their unit, including ordinary configs under standard systemd system directories. Exact duplicate file/package components within one service and two processes managing the same unit are also rejected. A process may own its unit file and multiple drop-ins.
For a reproducible file conflict, change the repository config target to /etc/vmango.conf in a copy of the example. Validation identifies the host and both vmango-repository/config.repository and vmango/config.main, including with --service vmango.
Selection --host, --tag, and --service can each repeat. Matching is exact and case sensitive. Unknown names produce errors; repeated selectors are harmless.
Within the host group, host names and tags form a union: --host gena --tag net selects gena plus every host tagged net. Repeated service names form a union of already assigned services. The host group and service group intersect. With no selectors in a group, that group selects everything. Selecting a service never assigns it to new hosts or adds dependencies. Selected hosts with no matching assignments remain visible with an empty services list. Hosts are displayed by name; their assignments are displayed by increasing service order. --tag selects hosts, and every selected host still receives services and variables from all its tags. Duplicate assignment, service-order, ownership and variable conflicts on unselected hosts are outside the scope; service selection cannot hide those conflicts on selected hosts. Definitions and references, including assignments in unused tags, are always validated. # All services on one host go run . inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml --host gena # One service on every host go run . inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml --service vmango # A union of hosts, intersected with a union of services go run . inventory show -i examples/inventory/richt.yaml \ --host gena --tag net --service vmango-repository --service vmango Secret declarations Named sources currently accept only {type: yaml, file: <local path>}. Paths are relative to the inventory file. Multiple independent YAML sources are allowed. A default source is required only when a template calls secret without naming a source. Inventory commands show declarations and never read the files or their values, even if a file exists; missing source files therefore do not fail inventory validation. Secret lookup and template secret evaluation belong to plan preparation. Sources are read locally on the machine running diff, including for SSH targets. An absent service does not render templates or read secret sources. See YAML secrets and sensitive files for the value schema, function arguments, caching, diagnostics, and saved-plan behavior.

body:
Build with make build. The example writes /var/tmp/richt-example/greeting.conf on the local machine:
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/files/inventory.yaml bin/richt diff -i examples/files/inventory.yaml bin/richt diff -i examples/files/inventory.yaml -o /var/tmp/richt-example-plan.json bin/richt apply /var/tmp/richt-example-plan.json bin/richt apply -y /var/tmp/richt-example-plan.json bin/richt apply -y -i examples/files/inventory.yaml diff reads and compares files without changing managed resources. It renders Go text/templates with the selected host’s resolved variables, and missing variables fail preparation. Template paths are relative to the service definition file. The secret function reads a string from a local YAML source and automatically marks the file sensitive. Standard Go template built-ins remain available, including printf, index, and slice. Parse and execution failures use generic diagnostics for every template so errors cannot quote template text or transformed secret values. Change greeting in the example to see an update; run a second diff after apply to see no changes. Set the assigned service’s state: absent and build a new plan to explicitly remove its managed file; removal does not open templates or secret sources.
A saved plan contains rendered text, unified patches, requested owner/group names, file attributes, and a progress entry per task. It stays executable after the source template, inventory, or secret source changes or disappears. Apply uses those exact inputs, writes the target file, and does not compare current file contents against the old diff. It creates necessary parent directories. Ordinary file access follows target and parent symlinks; removal unlinks the named file or symlink. Users and groups named by owner and group must exist on the target. Names are resolved during observation and again when applying attributes; changed numeric IDs between diff and apply are allowed. Unspecified ownership and permissions of existing files are preserved; new files default to mode 0644. Specify modes as quoted octal strings.
Set selinux: system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0 on a config to manage its full SELinux label on an SELinux-enabled Linux machine. The kernel must accept the label. The label is compared during diff and applied through the open target file descriptor. SELinux requests fail explicitly on other systems.
Without -y, apply requires a terminal and explicit y or yes; empty or negative answers cancel. Piped input does not count as a terminal. -y only skips confirmation. Host/tag/service filters and -i are accepted while building a plan and rejected when applying a saved plan.
Saved plan progress is written atomically before and after each task. The stable adjacent .lock file prevents simultaneous applies even while the JSON file is replaced. Plan and lock files use restrictive permissions. Keep the sidecar file; its existence alone does not mean an apply is running. Parent-directory aliases are resolved for locking. Hardlink aliases of saved plans are rejected. If a task fails, later tasks on that host are blocked and other hosts continue. Run apply explicitly again to retry unfinished tasks; successful tasks are skipped. Interrupted tasks can run again. There are no automatic retries or rollback. Hosts execute concurrently, with a default limit of 20. Use --parallelism N on every apply, including a saved plan; 1 executes sequentially. Tasks within each host remain ordered. A progress write failure stops admission of further actions globally; already running operations are awaited and may have taken effect. Without a plan file, progress exists only in memory and no plan is automatically saved.
Calling secret automatically marks the file sensitive; sensitive: false cannot override this. Use sensitive: true when old bytes also need protection after removing a secret call or declaring a service absent. There is no persistent secret history, and absent services do not render templates. Sensitive displays hide the entire old/new file diff, including context, and file operation error details. Actual bytes still determine changes and process reactions. These rules include owned units and drop-ins.
Saved JSON still contains the real rendered text and patch, including old secret bytes, so protect it as sensitive data. Plans, adjacent locks, and atomic plan replacements use mode 0600. Restrict access to the containing directory and do not publish plans or command captures as harmless artifacts. Sensitivity controls display, not target file permissions: new targets still default to mode 0644, so specify mode: "0600" for private files. The examples contain only fictional values. See YAML secrets and sensitive files and the isolated example .
New plans use strict JSON schema version 1.1. Legacy local 1.0 plans remain accepted with their numeric ownership fields; new connection and named-ownership fields require 1.1. Unknown fields, incompatible versions, invalid operations, and malformed progress are rejected. Plans are executable inputs: inspect their displayed changes and trust their source before confirmation. The file executor supports local and SSH targets, with optional noninteractive sudo. Explicit connection settings are stored in the plan; the system SSH client reads its current configuration on each invocation. See SSH and parallel apply . Unsupported transports and backends fail before changes. Results show completed, previously completed, failed, and blocked tasks per host, with the saved plan path for manual continuation.
Run local unit and CLI checks with go test ./.... On a disposable Linux machine with SELinux Enforcing, run the file acceptance suite as root:
python3 tests/integration/files.py --binary ./bin/richt --work-root /root --target-root /var/lib The suite allocates unique test directories beneath the specified existing roots and removes only those directories afterwards. --keep retains them for inspection. It verifies create/update/no changes/absent, ownership/mode/SELinux, frozen saved inputs, inode preservation, missing owner/group errors and ordinary symlink writes, partial progress and continuation, sensitive display, actual terminal confirmation, and concurrent apply locking. It does not install packages or manage services.
All 17 checks passed on 2026-11-01 on a disposable AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 host with SELinux Enforcing. This includes two independent YAML sources, multiline secret bytes, private plan permissions, continuation after deleting sources, requested target mode and SELinux label, and explicit sensitivity when replacing old secret content. The suite removes its temporary directories after completion.

body:
This config-only example requires a built bin/richt, a POSIX shell, and a writable /var/tmp. It needs no RPM, systemd, SSH, root, or external service. Run commands from the repository root. Inventory validation is safe by itself:
bin/richt inventory validate -i examples/continuation/inventory.yaml Allocate a fresh workspace and substitute its path into a copy of the inventory:
work=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/richt-continuation.XXXXXX) sed "s|/var/tmp/richt-continuation-example|$work/target|g" \ examples/continuation/inventory.yaml > "$work/inventory.yaml" bin/richt diff -i "$work/inventory.yaml" -o "$work/plan.json" The shared example tag assigns all three services. Their service definition orders 10, 20 and 30 determine execution. Diff prepares all three files while the target directory is absent. Create a regular file at the second file’s future parent path after preparation:
mkdir -p "$work/target" printf 'deliberate obstruction\n' > "$work/target/blocked" if bin/richt apply -y "$work/plan.json"; then echo 'Unexpected success: inspect the workspace before continuing.' else echo 'Expected failure: the second target has a regular file as its parent.' fi cat "$work/target/first.conf" test ! -e "$work/target/third.conf" The first service succeeds; the second fails; the third is blocked on that host. The saved JSON contains this progress. Remove only the deliberate obstruction and explicitly apply the same plan:
rm "$work/target/blocked" bin/richt apply -y "$work/plan.json" cat "$work/target/first.conf" "$work/target/blocked/second.conf" \ "$work/target/third.conf" bin/richt diff -i "$work/inventory.yaml" Continuation reports previously completed tasks and skips them, retries the unfinished second service, and then runs the third. The final diff has no changes. It does not rerender templates or recalculate the saved plan. A task interrupted after taking effect may run again; exactly-once execution is not guaranteed. There is no automatic retry or rollback.
To repeat, allocate another workspace. Once inspected, remove this run’s allocated directory and its plan/lock together:
rm -r "$work" Validation status: this walkthrough passed on AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 on 2026-11-01, including deletion of the inventory before explicit continuation. See the acceptance report for environment and scope.

title: Failure and continuation

body:
Richt manages each service in binary → config → process order. A service may contain any nonempty combination of these component sets. Services run in their definition’s order; tags supply assignments and after orders processes within one service. References and cycles are validated before diff. There are no cross-service dependency links.
The supported package backend is DNF 4, including its YUM 4 compatibility command. YUM 3, DNF 5, APT, and non-systemd process managers are unsupported. The end-to-end verification environment is AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64, DNF 4.20.0, YUM 4 compatibility, systemd 257, SELinux Enforcing. Other Linux versions have not been verified. manager --version is checked during preparation without reading repository metadata. Local and SSH transports are supported, including explicit noninteractive sudo. See SSH and parallel apply for connection and authentication rules.
Package requests binaries: app: type: rpm manager: dnf # dnf (default), or yum backed by DNF 4 package: richt-demo # RPM NAME, without an architecture selector version: 0:1.0-1.noarch # optional; epoch:version-release.arch An omitted version means install the package only if it is absent. An already installed package is left alone, even if a newer repository version exists. An explicit version includes all of epoch, version, release, and architecture; write epoch 0 explicitly when the package has no epoch. The installed RPM database determines whether the exact request already holds. An exact request uses dnf -y install-nevra -- NAME-EPOCH:VERSION-RELEASE.ARCH (or yum), allowing both upgrades and downgrades. An unversioned request uses install-n; removal uses remove. Package names and versions are validated as individual arguments. Local execution passes them directly; SSH safely quotes each argument for the target shell.
Diff reads the installed RPM database, without consulting repository metadata. A preceding config-only service can therefore create a .repo file that does not exist at diff time. The JSON plan already contains the package operation; apply does not add tasks or reconstruct the plan. The host downloads packages when that operation runs.
The plan fixes the requested package and exact NEVRA when specified. It does not freeze dependency resolution, repository metadata, RPM checksums, scriptlet side effects, or all packages in the transaction. Those are resolved by DNF on the target at execution. Repository trust and signature checking follow the host’s repository configuration. Large RPM artifacts are not embedded in JSON.
Process lifecycle processes: web: type: systemd unit: richt-demo.service state: running # running (default), or stopped enabled: true # omitted: preserve current enablement timeout: 5s # positive Go duration; default 5s restart_on: [binary.app] reload_on: [config.main] worker: type: systemd unit: richt-worker.service after: [web] Only resources whose diff actually changes contribute a reaction. Multiple reload requests combine into one reload; any restart request wins over reload. An unrelated changed resource has no reaction. Apply checks the process state immediately before its lifecycle task and chooses an already displayed branch:
Current state Target Input reaction Action inactive or failed running any or none start once active running restart restart once active running reload reload once active running none no action active stopped any or none stop once inactive or failed stopped any or none no action An unexpected load/activation state fails the task. There is no extra restart or reload after start. timeout must be a positive Go duration and defaults to 5s. A lifecycle command and its state verification form one persisted task. Start/reload/restart must reach active; stop must reach inactive or failed. Status is polled while waiting. The command and all waiting share one timeout; timeout and command errors stop that host, without retry or fallback. A timed-out systemctl client does not roll back a systemd job that was already accepted. An explicit continuation retries an unfinished task.
Enablement has its own task and saved progress. Changing enabled does not require starting, stopping, or restarting the process. A stopped process can remain enabled, and a running process can be disabled. Each enablement command and its verification also share the process timeout.
Owned units and drop-ins Without unit_file or overrides, Richt uses an existing unit, including one supplied by a managed RPM. Full units and drop-ins use the same templates, permissions, sensitivity, ownership, and SELinux rules as ordinary configs:
processes: main: type: systemd unit: richt-demo.service restart_on: [binary.app] reload_on: [config.main] overrides: 20-reload.conf: mode: "0644" template: inline: | [Service] ExecReload= ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID unit_file is a single Config object; its default path is /etc/systemd/system/<unit>. Each override key is a .conf basename and its default path is /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/<key>. Explicit paths must match these locations. Templates are resolved relative to the service definition.
Calling secret automatically makes a unit or drop-in sensitive, and the whole file diff is hidden. Real secret changes still schedule daemon reload and the normal process reaction. Set mode: "0600" when its target bytes must be private; sensitivity alone does not change target permissions. Use sensitive: true explicitly to protect old bytes after removing a secret call or declaring the service absent. Absent services do not open templates or secret sources. See YAML secrets and sensitive files .
Changes to owned units or drop-ins appear in the file diff. Richt schedules systemctl daemon-reload before process tasks, then a restart reaction for the process whose definition changed (or only start when it is stopped). Managed config files under systemd’s standard unit directories also schedule a daemon reload. Package installation with processes schedules daemon-reload so a previously missing package unit can be discovered without relying on RPM scriptlets.
A declared reload_on must be supported during preparation, even when its input does not currently change. Existing units use their effective unit fragment and drop-ins; prepared replacements are merged in systemd filename order using the maintained coreos/go-systemd parser. ExecReload resets are respected, as is Type=notify-reload. Reload is never silently converted to restart.
When the RPM and its unit do not exist yet, diff cannot inspect that future unit without downloading it from a repository that may not exist yet. A first installation with reload_on must therefore provide an owned full unit or drop-in declaring a supported ExecReload (as in the example). Otherwise preparation reports that reload capability cannot be verified. A first install using only restart reactions can use the package’s unit directly.
Removal and continuation For a service assignment with state: absent, processes are stopped and verified, then disabled, before owned units/drop-ins and declared configs are removed. Processes are stopped in reverse dependency order. Declared RPM packages are removed after the managed files, and a final daemon reload follows unit/drop-in or package changes. An already missing unit is accepted during removal. An external unit that remains installed is still stopped and disabled.
Across services, removal follows ascending service-definition order, just like present assignments. There is no automatic reverse service removal order.
DNF may remove dependent packages in its removal transaction. RPM itself controls the treatment of its package-owned config files, including possible .rpmsave files. Richt removes only explicitly declared config/unit/drop-in files; it does not purge application data, state directories, unrelated files, or .rpmsave files. Removing a tag or service assignment from inventory does not mean absent; declare absent to request deletion.
A failed task blocks later tasks on that host. Successful config writes and other task progress remain saved when applying a JSON file. A pending process reaction remains in that file, so continuation starts with the failed process task and does not re-render or rewrite completed configs. There is no automatic rollback, retry, autosaved plan, or run history.
Ready-package walkthrough For the current full local example, use ready vmango RPMs on a disposable DNF 4/systemd target. It covers repository configuration, package/config/process preparation, and explicit removal without creating a custom RPM. See validation for the results actually recorded for that scenario.
Developer fixture regression suite The following harness is a separate developer regression tool. Its custom RPM build prerequisites are not required by the ready-vmango walkthrough or current package acceptance.
Use a disposable AlmaLinux machine with root privileges. The fixture only manages resources named richt-*; the harness deliberately installs/removes its test package and changes its test units. Do not run it on a user host.
dnf install -y rpm-build createrepo_c python3 # Build Richt on the target, or copy a Linux binary built on another machine: # CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o richt . python3 examples/rpm-systemd/verify.py ./richt /root/richt-service-test The harness builds real versions 1.0-1 and 2.0-1 of a minimal noarch RPM, creates a file repository, and runs the CLI against it. It checks first install with a previously absent repo config, exact update/downgrade, no-op diff, unversioned policy, merged reactions, no extra restart after start, independent enablement and stopped state, multiple processes with after, command failure, a shared command/wait timeout, unsupported reload, persisted process resume, YUM 4 exact install/removal, and complete declared-resource removal. It also checks initial secret rendering and secret rotation, actual reload reactions, redacted file display, and frozen apply after deleting the secret source. The recorded fixture run passed all 33 checks on 2026-11-01 on the environment listed above; this is evidence for that fixture suite, not a verification claim for the ready-vmango example. Plans, displayed diffs, apply output, and acceptance.json remain in the work directory. Application event traces are deliberately retained. Fixture scripts require only standard Python and shell facilities in addition to the listed RPM build tools.
For a manual walkthrough:
sh examples/rpm-systemd/build-repository.sh ./richt diff -i examples/rpm-systemd/inventory.yaml -o /root/demo-plan.json ./richt apply -y /root/demo-plan.json ./richt diff -i examples/rpm-systemd/inventory.yaml Change version between 0:1.0-1.noarch and 0:2.0-1.noarch, or change the config inline content, to inspect the resulting exact package and process branches. Set the demo assignment to absent to remove it.
DNF’s exact installation behavior is documented in the DNF command reference . Unit states and systemctl operations follow the systemd 257 systemctl manual .

body:
Richt uses the system OpenSSH ssh executable. Existing ssh_config aliases, identity files, SSH agent, proxy/jump settings, and known-hosts policy remain in effect. The controller needs OpenSSH in PATH; remote targets need the Linux utilities used by the selected resources (GNU coreutils/findutils, getent, and, when requested, DNF 4/YUM 4, systemd, or SELinux tools). No Richt daemon or installed Richt binary is needed on an SSH target.
tags: application: services: application: {} services: application: {order: 10, file: services/application.yaml} hosts: - name: application-a tags: [application] transport: type: ssh host: app-a # address or existing ssh_config alias user: deploy # optional; otherwise use SSH configuration port: 2222 # optional; otherwise use SSH configuration sudo: true # explicit; never enabled implicitly host accepts a hostname, address, or SSH alias; use the separate user field instead of user@host or an SSH URI. Explicit host, user, and port select the destination and override client defaults. SSH configuration is read on every invocation. Saved plans keep these explicit inputs and the sudo flag, not a snapshot of resolved SSH options, keys, or passwords. Changes to ssh_config between diff and apply are allowed, including changes to the address behind an alias. Review the alias, explicit overrides, and privilege mode displayed before applying a plan.
SSH always runs in batch mode without a terminal. Richt does not prompt for login passwords, key passphrases, or host-key confirmation. Configure keys or load them into your agent beforehand, and establish host trust using your normal SSH workflow. The normal client host-key policy remains effective; Richt never disables verification. Authentication or trust failures fail the affected host. Client settings that replace the requested command, disable its session, or discard its stdin are overridden so the prepared operation can execute.
When sudo: true, target commands and file operations use sudo -n. Configure noninteractive privilege access for the required commands before preparing the plan. A password-required sudo policy fails rather than opening a prompt. sudo: false leaves the login user’s privileges unchanged. Local transport also accepts explicit sudo. apply -y skips only Richt’s plan confirmation; it does not enable interactive authentication or change privileges.
Files are read on the target during diff. Prepared content is sent through SSH stdin during apply, including for privileged writes; file content is never put into command arguments. Writes follow ordinary target and parent symlinks, and removal unlinks the named file or symlink. Owner/group names are resolved on the target at observation and again when attributes are applied. Changed numeric IDs are allowed. These rules also apply to local files. The saved file bytes, resource requests, task order, and process branches remain fixed; apply does not reread inventory/templates or recalculate changes.
YAML secret sources are read on the controller during preparation, including when writes use SSH or sudo. Apply and continuation use real saved bytes without reading those sources. Secret calls automatically hide the entire old/new file diff; explicit sensitive: true also protects old bytes when removing a secret call or a file. Set target mode: "0600" explicitly when required. Saved plans contain real secrets and use mode 0600, as do their locks and atomic replacements. See YAML secrets and sensitive files .
Parallel execution and continuation ./bin/richt diff -i examples/ssh/inventory.yaml -o /tmp/richt-plan.json ./bin/richt apply -y --parallelism 2 /tmp/richt-plan.json # Continue unfinished tasks, with a different limit: ./bin/richt apply -y --parallelism 1 /tmp/richt-plan.json Each apply handles at most 20 hosts concurrently by default. --parallelism N sets a positive limit for that run; 1 runs sequentially. The limit is not part of the saved plan and does not select hosts or alter tasks. Inventory/host/tag/ service filters remain forbidden when applying a saved plan. Local and SSH hosts can share one plan.
Services run by service-definition order, and tasks remain sequential within each host. A task failure blocks the rest of its host; other active and queued hosts continue. All hosts finish before the final ordered summary, and any failure produces a nonzero exit. Explicit continuation skips successful tasks and retries unfinished tasks. There are no automatic retries or rollback.
All task progress changes and atomic plan saves are synchronized. The adjacent lock still prevents two processes applying the same saved plan. A save failure stops admission of new actions globally. Already admitted actions are awaited and may have taken effect; interrupted unfinished tasks can run again on an explicit continuation. SSH client cancellation cannot guarantee that a command already accepted by the remote host stopped.
Developer fixture acceptance The following harness uses custom fixture RPMs for developer regressions. It is separate from the ready-vmango walkthrough and current package acceptance, which do not build RPMs. For a file-only SSH scenario, define configs with transport: {type: ssh, host: <alias>, sudo: true} and use the same diff/save/apply workflow without a package repository. See validation for newly recorded runs.
Use two isolated Linux SSH targets with their own RPM database, filesystem, and systemd instance. Both need an SSH alias, a non-root login with noninteractive sudo, and the fixture repository produced by build-repository.sh at /var/lib/richt-demo-fixture/repo. The test manages only its fixture resources, but installs/removes packages and services: use disposable targets.
The SSH harness records plans, command output, and an acceptance report. It also creates and removes a unique test user/group to verify ownership changes between preparation and apply. This stage needs the target shadow-utils commands (useradd, usermod, groupadd, groupmod, userdel, and groupdel). See its --help for target and output options. The local file harness and service harness remain regression checks; concurrency and persistence failures also have Go race-detector tests.
go test -race ./plan ./engine ./config ./transport ./cli python3 tests/integration/ssh.py --binary ./bin/richt \ --host-a richt-test-a --host-b richt-test-b \ --work-root /tmp/richt-ssh-acceptance The recorded fixture run on 2026-11-01 used two isolated AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 system containers, each running its own SSH server, systemd 257, filesystem, and DNF 4.20 RPM database, on a disposable SELinux-Enforcing Linux host. The 31 SSH harness checks passed with non-root logins, SSH-agent authentication, and noninteractive sudo. The 17 local file and 33 local RPM/systemd checks also passed.
The SSH run includes two independent YAML sources, automatic sensitivity, partial failure and continuation after deleting the source files, frozen multiline bytes, and mode 0600 on both targets. Secret bytes are checked by digest so reports do not contain their values. Both containers and the temporary SSH agent were stopped after verification; reports were retained.
A macOS controller also passed six secret checks through a non-root login to the enforcing Linux host with explicit sudo: controller-local sources, automatically hidden files, a deliberate partial failure after deleting sources, continuation that skips successful tasks, frozen multiline content, root-owned mode 0600 targets with the requested SELinux label, and private saved progress. Its unique temporary inputs and targets were removed after verification.
Earlier KRG-73 checks verified changed live SSH aliases, unknown/changed host-key rejection, password-required sudo failure, conflicting SSH session options, and local named UID/GID changes after preparation. A macOS controller prepared and applied a sensitive file with an explicit SELinux label on the Linux host, then observed no changes. Container isolation is not evidence of a separate kernel; SELinux file behavior was verified on the enforcing host itself.

body:
Secret values are fetched during plan preparation on the machine running diff or apply -i. Inventory inspection does not open secret sources, and applying a saved plan never fetches them again. Local files, SSH/sudo files, systemd units, and drop-ins use the same template and sensitivity rules.
Sources and lookup Declare independent named sources in inventory:
secret_sources: default: {type: yaml, file: secrets/default.yaml} production: {type: yaml, file: secrets/production.yaml} Paths are relative to the inventory file, regardless of the target transport. Only local YAML sources are supported; environment variables and external secret stores are outside the current implementation. Inventory commands show declarations without checking whether the declared files exist or are valid.
A source contains one YAML mapping. Nested mappings provide dot-separated key access. Mapping keys must be nonempty strings without dots. Leaf values must be strings, including empty strings and multiline strings; quote numeric, boolean, or date-like values when they should be strings. Empty mappings are accepted but do not resolve to string values. For example, these values are fictional:
database: password: "fictional-example-password" numeric-token: "123" optional: "" message: | fictional first line fictional second line Lists, numbers, booleans, dates, nulls, duplicate keys, aliases, YAML merges, custom tags, malformed YAML, and multiple documents are rejected. The entire selected source is validated on first use, including keys not requested by the template. Sources not used by the selected preparation remain unopened.
password={{ secret "database.password" }} production={{ secret "database.password" "production" }} quoted={{ printf "%q" (secret "database.password" "production") }} secret accepts one string key and an optional string source name. An omitted source selects the name default; an explicit source selects only that source. There is no merging, search, or fallback. Identical keys in different sources are independent. A missing selected source, invalid key, missing leaf key, unreadable source, or invalid source fails preparation. default need not be declared when every call selects another existing source explicitly. Lookup keys cannot contain empty segments, so .password, database., and a..b are invalid.
Each selected source is loaded once per diff. Its values or load failure remain cached for that preparation across files and hosts; a new diff loads afresh. An absent service does not render templates or read secret sources.
Templates and diagnostics Templates retain the standard Go text/template built-ins and control flow. For example, printf can format a secret, index and slice can select part of a string, and html, js, or urlquery can escape it. No command execution, environment lookup, or external fetching function is added.
Any executed secret call makes the entire file sensitive, even when its value is transformed, assigned to a template variable, or omitted from output. sensitive: false cannot disable automatic marking. Parse and execution errors are generic for all templates; Richt does not print source snippets, function arguments, source names, keys, secret values, or underlying YAML decoder details from secret lookup failures. This also protects failures raised by standard built-ins after a secret has been transformed.
Display, saved inputs, and permissions A sensitive file display shows its path and fact of change while hiding both old and new content and all patch context. File operation diagnostics are generic. Comparison still uses real bytes, so changed secrets trigger configured process reactions. Ordinary config, owned-unit, and drop-in rules all apply.
Use explicit sensitive: true when replacing old secret content with a template that no longer calls secret, or when removing a secret-bearing file with state: absent. There is no persistent secret history. Removal skips template evaluation, so a secret call in the unused template cannot automatically mark the removal sensitive.
Saved JSON is executable data and contains real rendered contents and patches, including old secret bytes. Sensitivity is persisted, but display placeholders never replace executable inputs. Apply and explicit continuation use the saved bytes after inventory, templates, and source files change or disappear; completed tasks are skipped as usual. Inspect human-readable plan output and protect the JSON itself.
Plans, locks, and atomic plan replacements use mode 0600. Keep their containing directory private and do not publish the JSON, logs, or temporary artifacts. Target permissions follow the file contract: a new file defaults to mode 0644, and existing permissions are preserved unless specified. Set mode: "0600" explicitly for a private target. For SSH/sudo, prepared bytes travel through stdin instead of command arguments; sources remain on the controller.
When a sensitive file has an explicit mode, its write first restricts the target to owner-only read/write access (0600), before writing content. The following attribute operation applies the requested final permissions and ownership. A failed write can leave the target at 0600 until explicit continuation. This applies to new and existing files, locally and over SSH/sudo, without replacing the inode. Without an explicit mode, the usual default and preserved-permission rules still apply.
Local RPM/systemd and SSH/sudo command failures retain safe failure categories and exit status, but omit command output that could contain secret-bearing application diagnostics. Temporary plan files are cleaned up on completion or handled failures; forced termination can leave a private temporary file behind.
The two-source example verifies lookup, redaction, private files, and frozen saved inputs without printing their contents. On 2026-11-01, the expanded suites passed 17 local file, 33 RPM/systemd, and 31 SSH/sudo checks on AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 with DNF 4.20 and systemd 257. Local file checks ran with SELinux Enforcing; two isolated system containers supplied the SSH targets with non-root logins and noninteractive sudo. These runs verified real secret-change reloads, frozen multiline bytes, private file modes, and continuation after source deletion. Containers share the host kernel; SELinux labels were verified on the enforcing host itself.

body:
Save a plan before applying when you need progress to survive the invocation:
./bin/richt diff -i inventory.yaml -o plan.json ./bin/richt apply plan.json # Fix the external cause of a failure, then explicitly continue: ./bin/richt apply plan.json The runnable config-only example deliberately fails after an earlier file succeeds, fixes the local filesystem cause, and continues the same plan. It needs no package installation or process manager. Follow its commands and cleanup instructions in a fresh temporary directory.
What is recorded Each task records running before execution, then success only after its result checks pass, or failure. Saved progress is atomically written to that same JSON file. A stable adjacent .lock file prevents simultaneous applies of the same plan; keep it in place. Its mere existence does not mean a process holds the lock. Plan, lock, and atomic replacement files use mode 0600. Parent-directory aliases resolve to the same lock; hardlink aliases of plans are rejected.
If a task fails, the rest of that host is blocked, including later services. Other active and queued hosts continue. A later explicit apply skips successful tasks and retries unfinished tasks in their original order. A successful config write is therefore not repeated just to reach a failed process reaction.
An interrupted task may already have changed its target and can run again. Exactly-once execution is not guaranteed. A failure to save progress stops admission of further actions globally; in-flight operations are awaited and may already have taken effect. Forced termination may leave private temporary plan files behind and may prevent the final report.
Frozen inputs and checks Continuation uses the original prepared inputs. It does not reread inventory, templates, or secret sources, rerender files, recalculate differences, or check for intervening resource drift. Successful tasks are not rechecked. Editing the inventory after a failure does not change a saved task. Fix an external prerequisite and continue, or deliberately prepare a new plan when the desired inputs have changed; review that new plan separately.
Process state reads for a prepared branch and result verification still happen during execution. Owner/group names are resolved again on the target. SSH uses the system client’s current configuration, including an alias’s current address. The saved explicit connection inputs remain fixed. DNF resolves dependencies and repository transactions when its prepared package request executes. These are the documented boundaries of frozen inputs; see files and saved plans , services , and SSH .
Confirmation and concurrency Every invocation displays the plan and requires terminal agreement unless -y is supplied. Piping a response is not agreement; -y only skips the prompt. You can change --parallelism for continuation, including setting it to 1, without changing selected hosts, tasks, or saved inputs. Inventory/host/tag/ service filters are rejected with a saved plan.
Without a plan file, apply -i inventory.yaml holds plan and progress only in memory. Nothing is automatically saved; a later invocation prepares a new plan. Richt has no automatic retries, rollback, separate progress database, attempt history, or automatic replay of completed tasks.

body:
Richt currently implements local/SSH transport, explicit noninteractive sudo, strict local YAML inventory, RPM through DNF 4/YUM 4, systemd, local templates, and local YAML secret sources. See installation and validation for requirements and verified platforms. YUM 3, DNF 5, APT, non-systemd managers, URL inventory/templates, direct binary URL downloads, and external secret stores are unsupported.
Executable plans are prepared inputs A saved plan fixes selected hosts, explicit connection inputs, task order, operations, file bytes/patches/attributes, package requests, and allowed process branches. Apply does not reread inventory/templates/secrets, compute a new diff, or check for drift. A file changed by another actor after diff can be overwritten by the prepared write. Completed tasks are skipped without rechecking them on continuation. Reprepare and review when you want current observations.
These inputs retain defined execution-time dependencies:
OpenSSH reads current client configuration and credentials. An alias may now resolve to a different address; the plan display states this policy. Owner/group names are resolved again on the target, and their numeric IDs may have changed. DNF resolves repository metadata, dependencies, and the transaction at apply. A pinned NEVRA fixes the explicit package request, not RPM checksums, scriptlets, every dependency, or repository trust configuration. RPM artifacts are not embedded in the plan. Process tasks read current state to select a prepared branch and verify the result. Running means systemd active, not application readiness. Ordinary file operations follow target and parent symlinks; removal unlinks the named entry. There is no special symlink prohibition or inode identity contract. Named users/groups must exist. File parents are created as needed, but their permissions are not independently declared resources.
Failure and removal There are no automatic retries, rollback, autosaved plans, separate progress stores, or run/attempt history. An interrupted operation can have taken effect before its success was saved, and explicit continuation can execute it again. A failed host blocks its remaining tasks while other hosts continue. See continuation .
Process command and verification polling share a positive duration, default 5s. Timeouts fail the task; an accepted systemd job may continue after the client times out. Unsupported reload is an error and never falls back to restart. Services follow service-definition order; process after works only inside one service. There is no cross-service dependency graph or automatic dependency selection.
state: absent removes explicitly owned resources in the documented order. Deleting an assignment alone does not remove anything. DNF can remove dependent packages and RPM can retain .rpmsave files. Richt does not purge application data, state directories, unrelated files, or .rpmsave. It does not validate an application’s configuration before writing it.
Secrets and future scope Human-readable sensitive displays hide entire old/new file diffs and context; raw JSON retains real rendered bytes and patches, including old secrets. Plans and locks use 0600; target file permissions are separately configured. Use mode: "0600" for private targets and sensitive: true when protecting old content during removal or after removing a secret call. No persistent secret history exists. See secrets .
NetBox inventory and rendering integration, agents, central run history, fleet rollout orchestration, additional package/process backends, application configuration validation, and external secret stores remain later scope. They are not prerequisites or shipped CLI features.
