Acceptance on 2026-11-01 passed on two authorized disposable AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 hosts with DNF 4.20.0, systemd 257, Python 3.12.13 and SELinux Enforcing. The controller was macOS with the system OpenSSH client; remote execution used a non-root account with explicit passwordless sudo -n. Both targets had independent RPM databases, filesystems and systemd instances.
The tested source was revision 187f67a62a09179e0f5e2c01c918e3341aeb102d plus the current documentation and example changes. The coordinator’s make check passed before transfer. Both binaries reported richt dev. Binary SHA-256 identities were:
Binary SHA-256 macOS controller d07ed96789b60d4c8aee7bbca1185c30cecc2b8c314be8fd35273db6a77fc225 Linux amd64 target 40335cbccfa7e4dc51604d1ef6e579d94e7292f8a8c6aa278859613a4b2e6feb The Linux binary was cross-built and transferred with the example sources. It was executed on Linux; a Go installation or target-side build was not tested.
Files, secrets and saved plans These commands passed on host A as root:
python3 tests/integration/files.py --binary ./bin/richt --work-root /root --target-root /var/lib python3 examples/secrets/verify.py ./bin/richt The file suite passed all 17 checks: create/update/no-op/explicit absence, root ownership, requested modes and SELinux labels, symlink behavior, missing owner/group rejection, frozen saved inputs, inode preservation, sensitive displays, partial failure and manual continuation, terminal confirmation, and same-plan apply locking. Its secret checks cover independent YAML sources, multiline bytes, private plans and continuation without source files.
The standalone secret example passed all four verification groups, including source/template/inventory deletion before apply and explicit-sensitive removal. Its private temporary files and the file suite’s allocated directories were removed automatically.
The quickstart shell commands passed on Linux using the transferred binary in place of make build and explicit apply -y for noninteractive execution: create, no-op, update and removal all succeeded. The continuation walkthrough produced the expected second-service failure, blocked later work and successful explicit continuation. Its inventory was deleted before continuation to additionally verify frozen inputs. The separate file suite exercised actual terminal agreement and cancellation.
Published RPM and local systemd lifecycle The Vmango walkthrough used published signed RPMs from the COPR rhel-10-x86_64 repository, with signature checking enabled. The repository and Vmango were absent before preparation. CRB was already enabled. The first apply wrote the repository file, then failed dependency resolution because genisoimage was unavailable without EPEL. After:
dnf install -y epel-release an explicit apply of the same saved plan skipped the successful repository write and installed Vmango. The examples now document CRB and EPEL prerequisites. No package was rebuilt to work around this dependency.
Private copies of the example were used for the following passed scenarios:
Scenario Observed result Install 0:0.16.0-1.el10.x86_64 RPM version matched; unit active and enabled; loopback HTTP request succeeded Repeat diff No changes Omit version while 0.17 was available No changes; installed version remained 0.16 Exact upgrade to 0:0.17.0-1.el10.x86_64 RPM version matched; active/enabled and HTTP checks passed Exact downgrade to 0:0.16.0-1.el10.x86_64 RPM version matched; active/enabled and HTTP checks passed Change log_level from info to debug Restart branch applied; systemd InvocationID changed; HTTP and subsequent no-op checks passed Request stopped and enabled Process inactive while enablement remained enabled Request running and disabled Process active while enablement was disabled Restore enabled, then declare both services absent Stop/disable completed; managed config, repository and RPM removed; subsequent diff had no changes Each mutation used bin/richt diff -i INVENTORY -o PLAN followed by bin/richt apply -y PLAN. Runtime checks used rpm -q, systemctl is-active, systemctl is-enabled, systemctl show -p InvocationID and curl --fail --silent --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:18080/. The HTTP check confirms an HTTP response, not hypervisor functionality or an authenticated application deployment. No clouds, login users or hypervisors were configured.
Two real SSH targets The SSH example was copied with explicit target addresses, user: almalinux and sudo: true. On the macOS controller:
bin/richt diff -i INVENTORY -o PLAN bin/richt apply -y --parallelism 2 PLAN bin/richt diff -i INVENTORY Both hosts installed published Vmango 0.16, reached active/enabled state, served loopback HTTP and then produced a no-op diff. A separate absent plan, also applied with parallelism 2, stopped/disabled and removed the package, managed config and repository on both targets.
A separate temporary config-only inventory exercised two independent local YAML secret sources across the same SSH targets. Its sources, template and inventory were deleted after diff and before apply. A deliberate parent-path obstruction on host A caused its second service to fail after the first succeeded; its third service was blocked. Host B completed all three services. After removing the obstruction, explicit continuation of that same plan completed host A and skipped all successful tasks on both hosts. Deliberate external edits to already successful files remained untouched, proving those writes were skipped. Frozen secret bytes, target mode 0600, private plan/lock modes and redacted CLI displays were verified. All six tasks ultimately had saved success status. Temporary remote targets were then removed.
Cleanup and limits Final checks on both hosts found no installed Vmango package, no managed /etc/vmango.conf or repository file, and a not-found/inactive Vmango unit. SELinux remained Enforcing. Neither rpm-build nor createrepo_c was installed at preflight or completion.
Package removal left about 12 KiB of generated application state under /var/lib/vmango on each host, including generated signing material. Host A also retained a package-generated /etc/vmango.conf.rpmnew after the version changes. EPEL release/policy packages, imported RPM signing keys and package manager caches were retained; DNF removed the genisoimage dependency during package removal. Private source copies, command captures and executable plans remain outside the tracked repository for review. They are not published with this documentation.
No custom RPM was built. The custom richt-demo suites (examples/rpm-systemd/verify.py and the full tests/integration/ssh.py) were deliberately excluded from this run. Their fixture-specific reload, timeout, changed-identity and YUM scenarios are not established by this report. This run also does not establish behavior on other distributions or DNF versions.
Tag assignments and service order, 2026-11-02 KRG-91 was verified on three independent disposable AlmaLinux 10.2 x86_64 hosts with SELinux Enforcing, DNF 4.20.0 and systemd 257. The macOS controller used non-root SSH logins and explicit sudo: true. CRB was already enabled; EPEL was initially absent on the PostgreSQL host and present on the two package hosts. Firewalld was inactive, so no firewall changes were required.
The source was revision aaa56d175b1ef22e6826b131591b5820b6c5e198 plus the KRG-91 working-tree changes. Tested binary SHA-256 identities were:
Binary SHA-256 macOS controller 905855e589a6422048b39d04c0c2d53446b361458e904e857a9f21537693d191 Linux amd64 a5d360a89c4abe442aae009d517421aa207b17e2cf9f97d6b539d1db23bd3f61 The updated Linux file harness passed all 17 checks, and the secret example passed all four groups. The updated quickstart passed create, no-op, update and explicit removal on Linux using the transferred binary and apply -y. Local make check and make docs-check passed; inventory validate/show smoke checks covered every checked-in example. Go regression tests cover inherited ordering, duplicate and ownership failures before service filtering, strict source validation, saved inputs, failure blocking and explicit continuation.
Three-host workload The standard-library driver tag_services.py generates private inventory, bare templates, a YAML secret source and saved plans. Run it only against explicitly authorized disposable hosts. The following names are illustrative; supply the authorized addresses or SSH aliases:
make build python3 tests/integration/tag_services.py --binary ./bin/richt \ --work-root /tmp/richt-tag-services \ --postgres-host postgres-test.example \ --kubernetes-host kubernetes-test-a.example \ --kubernetes-host kubernetes-test-b.example Targets need trusted host keys, noninteractive sudo, Python 3, curl, ss, enabled CRB, network access to the package repositories and an unused PostgreSQL data directory. This fixture requires inactive firewalld; prepare an equivalent isolated network policy separately when using a firewall. --user defaults to almalinux; use --postgres-address when the SSH name is not a database address reachable from the Kubernetes hosts. The fixture does not build custom RPMs. Kubernetes and CRI-O use their official v1.36 repositories, as described by Kubernetes and CRI-O ; repository and RPM signature checks remain enabled.
Assignments came exclusively from tags. All hosts had one shared monitoring tag assigning EPEL setup (service order 5) and node exporter (50). Kubernetes hosts also received repository configuration (10) and packages (30) from the kubernetes tag; the PostgreSQL host received its service (40) from the postgresql tag. Resolved services and saved tasks followed service order. --tag monitoring selected all three hosts, and --service node-exporter resolved exactly one assignment on each.
Resource Installed version or verified state PostgreSQL server/client 16.15-1.el10_2.x86_64 on the database host; client also installed on both Kubernetes hosts kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl 1.36.6-150500.1.1.x86_64 on both Kubernetes hosts CRI-O 1.36.7-150500.1.1.x86_64 on both Kubernetes hosts node-exporter 1.12.1-1.el10_2.x86_64 on all three hosts epel-release 10-6.el10.noarch on all three hosts PostgreSQL unit postgresql.service, active and enabled Exporter unit Managed through node_exporter.service, an alias of prometheus-node-exporter.service; active and enabled on all hosts kubelet unit Inactive and disabled on both hosts No kubeadm command was invoked, no cluster was initialized or joined, and CRI-O coverage establishes package installation rather than container runtime functionality. Each exporter returned HTTP 200 and node_uname_info at http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics.
PostgreSQL initialized a fresh test cluster through an owned systemd oneshot unit. Its effective settings were listen_addresses = '0.0.0.0' and password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256'; ss confirmed 0.0.0.0:5432. The external HBA file contained only local peer authentication and host all all 192.168.0.0/16 scram-sha-256, with no earlier password bypass. Both Kubernetes hosts connected to the dedicated richt_krg91 database and role using the correct generated password and failed password authentication with an incorrect one. A boolean database query verified the stored role password was SCRAM. The password entered through secret, remained in a root-owned mode-0600 SQL file and private executable inputs, and was excluded from displays and reports. External PostgreSQL config files received the postgresql_etc_t SELinux label; SELinux remained Enforcing throughout.
Fixture correction, continuation and retained state The first saved apply completed both Kubernetes hosts but PostgreSQL startup failed with 203/EXEC: the fixture initially used /usr/bin/postmaster, while the installed package provides /usr/bin/postgres. Inspection of the packaged unit identified the mismatch. A separate config-only Richt plan repaired the drop-in and reloaded systemd; the fixture now uses the verified path. Explicit apply of the original saved plan skipped successful tasks, retried PostgreSQL startup, bootstrapped the test role and completed monitoring. All 44 original tasks ended in success. No backend or saved-plan format change was needed.
The driver’s --verify-existing mode then passed its runtime assertions and saved a private final no-op plan with zero tasks on each host. This mode requires the original private work directory and matching target options, performs probes and diff without apply, and preserves the initial report and logs. Commands used for correction and continuation were:
bin/richt diff -i REPAIR.yaml -o REPAIR.json bin/richt apply -y REPAIR.json bin/richt apply -y --parallelism 3 FIRST-PLAN.json # Repeat the driver invocation with the same paths/targets and: # --verify-existing Retained resources include the installed packages and repositories, node exporter on all hosts, PostgreSQL data/test role/database, its external configs, private bootstrap SQL and initialization/bootstrap oneshot units. The file harness retained its uniquely named inputs and targets for inspection; the standalone secret example and quickstart removed their temporary resources. Private controller evidence retains inventories, secret source, executable plans/progress, original failure, repair and continuation logs, verification results and actual target identities outside the tracked repository. Restore the disposable hosts and choose an empty work directory before a fresh workload run. The custom RPM/systemd and full SSH fixture suites were not rerun; their inputs were updated and validated locally.
